pr_title: *: reduce object allocation by reuse chunk column
pr_body:
<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Reduce object allocation by reuse the chunk column.
Close #28340

Problem Summary:

For every query, we will create the chunk...
This is unnecessary, after the chunk data is drained by the MySQL client, nobody will use the chunk again, so it should be safe to reuse the chunk.

### What is changed and how it works?

Many changes... maybe I should split the PR to the lib and the use of the lib?

- Add a `chunkAlloc` for each client connection, allocate chunks from it, and reset for reuse after chunk sent to the client
- Add a `NewChunkFromAllocator` method to the `ResultSet` interface
- Update of the benchmark tests to use the chunk allocator
- Implementation of the chunk Allocator

For the chunk Allocator implementation, I decouple the chunk object into chunk column objects for reuse, because the Chunk differs a lot, while the chunk column are fix sized.

Allocating chunk will try to take a empty `Chunk` object from the `free` list, and fill the columns from the `columnAlloc`, 
and after reset, `allocated` chunks will turn into `free` with their columns collected into the poolColumnAllocator:

```
type allocator struct {
	allocated   []*Chunk
	free        []*Chunk
	columnAlloc poolColumnAllocator
}
```

issue_context.title: Chunk column reuse
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

Currently, TiDB allocation cause too much burden to the Go GC, and slow down the program.

Prepare plan cache can help a lot to reduce the allocation, unfortunately we still can not take full advantage of it.
I reported this issue https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/26868 in the past.
@qw4990 and @Reminiscent is handling it and we wish to make it GA soon.

Prepare plan cache ranks top1 in reducing the allocation.
So after that, I find chunk allocation also accounts a lot.

If we can reuse the chunk column, it may reduce the object allocation.

Chunk columns are feasible for reuse, as you can see they are fix sized depending on the field type, and there is no complex structure in it, only slice of bytes:

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/955274fbb138f721e729b446b41b104f1e7f0e7e/util/chunk/column.go#L63-L84
comments:
We have `localColumnPool` in `expression/builtin_vectorized.go`. So when enabled `tidb_enable_vectorized_expression`, it will reuse column chunk. 
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/cc524af1b23ee00a27df8af62020c6b7e8bd0d85/expression/builtin_vectorized.go#L36-L73

The implemention use `sync.Pool` to cache chunk column which will be recycled in 2 GC duration. It is introduced by #26078, not sure included in your test or not.

I'm not sure we need a true mempool for `chunk column` or not, because I can't reproduce high usage in `chunk column` right now. @tiancaiamao
I guess it's for the OLAP query, and OLTP can't benefit from it. @Defined2014

I found the old picture, the motivation for this issue:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1420062/138708290-86db1df6-4786-438d-9c05-1b23b6537f2e.png)

We already have the code `localColumnPool` in `expression/builtin_vectorized.go`,
but as you can see, it doesn't eliminate the chunk allocation.
I think maybe we can test the changes in the bank workload to verify it. @dbsid

review_comments: Do we need call 'Reset' when drainRecordSet failed and returns an err?

No, the `Reset()` is called after each query finish.
When `drainRecordSet` returns an err, the query will finish and run there.
